correctness.rationale: For each n>=3, F^3-fixed states are in bijection with closed n-walks of an explicit 512-vertex directed history graph whose edges are specified by nine Boolean majority checks. The complete exhaustive 512^2 test, Tarjan-equivalent two-pass SCC certificate and independent reachability check prove only three cyclic components, containing two fixed uniform, six fixed nonuniform, and six rotating nonuniform histories; all other 498 cannot occur in closed walks. The rotating six-by-six matrix is explicitly printed, has exact integer-verified characteristic polynomial z(z-2)(z^2-z+1)(z^2+3z+3), and yields the claimed exact trace. Closed walks of lengths 2 and 3 based at one vertex generate all n>=2. Original-rule direct simulation over every initial binary state n=3,4,5,6 independently confirms all periods and F=R for three-cycles. The finite certificate is part of the complete proof, rather than an infinite inference from finite samples.

originality.rationale: The closest same-automaton three-row public manuscript is exclusively a fixed-state census: its proof and explicit limitations do not classify least-period-three points. The adjacent two-row Toom result is a basin/Ising theorem on a different finite cylinder. Primary works on Toom ground states, noisy dynamics, erosion, and general finite automaton transfer methods do not give this exact three-row vertical-rotation rigidity or its explicit temporal three-cycle trace polynomial. The three-row result is not a corollary of the fixed-state count alone. All this is a best-knowledge claim with residual inaccessible-primary-text priority risk; no independent novelty certification is asserted.
residual_risks: The full 1997 ground-state paper was not obtainable, so an unindexed or unexamined historical parallel could exist.

A general 1988 periodic-cylinder transfer method is algorithmically applicable but does not itself establish the explicit special result; this contribution is a specialised computation and structural theorem.
Novelty is a reasoned source comparison, not a comprehensive guarantee across all inaccessible literature.

value.rationale: The three-row torus is the minimal nontrivial vertical periodic geometry with a genuine order-three spatial rotation. Classifying the entire least-temporal-period-three set for this canonical nonlinear automaton answers a natural dynamical-systems question not resolved by the known fixed-point or two-row basin counts. The structural exclusion of exotic three-cycles, exact positive formula at all circumferences and 2^n/3 asymptotic census are meaningful all-length dynamical invariants, not a finite computational table.
